meta.title: Data Advantage Audit
meta.core_finding: The bottleneck is information, not algorithms. Raw market probabilities (LL 0.959) outperform all ELASTICO models (best XGB Combined LL 1.100).

data_quality.source: Match results (goals) + shots_on_target proxy for xG
data_quality.critical_note: xg_for_home/away/diff are PROXY values (shots_on_target * 0.1), NOT real xG

xg_for_home.impact: HIGH - xG is fundamental to modern football analytics

missing: Post-shot xG (quality of shots on target)
feature_information_gap.independence_from_market: HIGH - real xG is a different information source from bookmaker odds
feature_information_gap.rationale: Real xG is the single most impactful missing data. The current proxy (SOT * 0.1) has no theoretical basis. Real xG measures chance quality, which bookmakers use internally but don't expose. Independent xG could provide genuine football intelligence the market doesn't fully reveal.

feature_information_gap.independence_from_market: VERY HIGH - injury news breaks after initial odds are set, creating timing advantage
feature_information_gap.rationale: Injuries are arguably the highest-value missing data. When a star player is ruled out 24-48 hours before kickoff, this information moves the market. If ELASTICO can ingest injury data EARLIER or more comprehensively than bookmakers incorporate it, this creates a genuine information advantage. The frontend already has an InjuryAdjustment system in the prediction engine, but no automated data feed.

feature_information_gap.independence_from_market: MEDIUM - tactical info partially reflected in odds
feature_information_gap.rationale: Tactical information is interesting but hard to quantify and partially captured by form/goal statistics. Formation changes and pressing style can affect outcomes, but bookmakers likely account for this in their models. Value is primarily in detecting tactical shifts early.

missing: Travel distance (for away teams in Europe)
Competition importance (league vs cup vs dead rubber)
Home advantage magnitude (crowd size, stadium familiarity)
International break impact (return from national team duty)
feature_information_gap.independence_from_market: MEDIUM-HIGH - some context factors are underweighted by bookmakers
feature_information_gap.rationale: Rest days and fixture congestion are known to affect performance. Referee tendencies (cards, penalties) are publicly available but not systematically used. Managerial changes create short-term unpredictability. Weather is available from weather APIs. These are moderate-value additions that are easy to acquire.

missing: Defensive actions (interceptions, blocks, tackles) by zone
feature_information_gap.independence_from_market: MEDIUM-HIGH - event-level data is not directly visible in odds
feature_information_gap.rationale: Event-level data enables computing real xG, xT, PPDA, and other advanced metrics. The frontend already has shot map and xT visualizations scaffolded (for StatsBomb demo data). This is the raw material needed for the EXPECTED PERFORMANCE and TACTICAL categories. Without event data, most advanced metrics are impossible.

missing: Odds movement timeline (odds at T-7d, T-3d, T-1d, T-6h)
Market timing signals (early vs late moves)
Steam move detection (systematic, not just on-demand)
feature_information_gap.independence_from_market: LOW - this IS market data, but with temporal dimension
feature_information_gap.rationale: The current system only uses CLOSING odds. Opening vs closing odds movement is a powerful feature. Steam moves and sharp action detection code EXISTS in odds_service.py and market_signals.py but is never used in training. If historical opening odds were available, this could create time-series features showing how the market reacts to information, which is a different kind of intelligence.

currently_available: ESPN news headlines (not piped to training)
missing: Transfer news (new signing impact, departure impact)
feature_information_gap.independence_from_market: HIGH - news timing creates genuine information asymmetry
feature_information_gap.rationale: News is the primary driver of late odds movement. If ELASTICO can systematically capture and encode news sentiment, it could detect information shifts before they're fully reflected in odds. However, NLP-based sentiment features are noisy and hard to validate. Best approach: structured injury/lineup news first, unstructured sentiment later.

data_source_capability_matrix.integration_gap: Service exists but data is never piped into the ML training pipeline. Adding pipeline integration is moderate effort.
No code exists. Requires web scraping or unofficial API. Reliability is uncertain. But provides FREE historical xG data for 5 major leagues 2014-present.
Frontend has demo code for one match. Open data is limited to specific tournaments. Full access requires enterprise license.
Service and signal detection exist. Historical odds endpoint exists but is not systematically collected or stored. No historical odds in training data.
CSVs already contain opening odds (B365, WH, etc.) and referee data that are NOT currently used. Can be extracted in Phase 2 pipeline without new API integration.
Injuries endpoint exists in ESPN API but is not called by the service. News is fetched but not used in training.
No code exists. Requires web scraping. Data is free and comprehensive. Historical depth is excellent.

prioritized_data_gaps.rationale: API-Football already has an injuries endpoint that is fully implemented but not called. This is the lowest-hanging fruit with highest potential value. Injury news creates market movement, and if captured systematically, could provide genuine independent signal. The frontend already has an InjuryAdjustment system waiting for real data.

experiment_design.treatment: Market + Football features + Injury features (key_player_absent_binary, squad_strength_pct, days_until_return_for_doubtful)
experiment_design.methodology: Temporal out-of-sample, same 5 windows as Phase 3.5/5
experiment_design.success_criterion: LL improvement > 0.01 over Raw Market in at least 3/5 windows

prioritized_data_gaps.rationale: Current xG proxy (SOT * 0.1) has no theoretical validation. Real xG measures chance quality, which is a genuinely different signal from goals scored. Understat provides free historical xG for all 5 current leagues. This is the most impactful data quality improvement possible.

experiment_design.treatment_1: Replace xG_PROXY with Understat real xG in all xG-dependent features
experiment_design.methodology: Temporal out-of-sample, same 5 windows. Compare Football-only XGB with proxy xG vs real xG. Then compare Combined (with market) vs Market-only.
experiment_design.success_criterion: Football-only model with real xG must beat Football-only with proxy xG by > 0.02 LL. Then Combined must beat Raw Market in at least 2/5 windows.

prioritized_data_gaps.estimated_cost: FREE (already in CSVs for some bookmakers)
prioritized_data_gaps.historical_availability: 5 seasons in existing CSVs (B365, PS, WH opening vs closing)
prioritized_data_gaps.rationale: The CSV files already contain both opening and closing odds for multiple bookmakers (B365H/B365CH, PSH/PSCH, etc.). These are currently IGNORED. The Odds API has historical odds endpoints. Market signal detection code EXISTS in odds_service.py. This requires zero new API integrations — just feature engineering from existing data.

experiment_design.baseline: Current best model (Raw Market LL 0.959, using closing odds only)
experiment_design.treatment_1: Add odds_movement_pp (closing - opening implied prob) as features
experiment_design.treatment_2: Add bookmaker_disagreement (std dev across bookmakers) as feature
experiment_design.treatment_3: Replace closing odds with opening odds and let model learn movement
experiment_design.methodology: Temporal OOS, same 5 windows. Critical: odds movement features must be computed BEFORE match time (no lookahead).
experiment_design.success_criterion: Combined model with odds movement must beat Raw Market closing odds in at least 2/5 windows.

prioritized_data_gaps.rationale: Knowing the starting XI allows computing pre-match squad strength metrics (sum of player ratings, absence of key positions). API-Football has a lineups endpoint. However, lineups are only confirmed close to kickoff, limiting pre-match prediction utility. Expected lineups (from news) are more useful for pre-match prediction.

experiment_design.baseline: Best model after Injuries + xG experiments
experiment_design.treatment: Add expected/confirmed lineup features (squad_strength_ratio, key_position_filled, formation_matchup)
experiment_design.methodology: Temporal OOS. Limit to matches where lineup data is available >2h before kickoff.
experiment_design.success_criterion: LL improvement > 0.005 over baseline in at least 2/5 windows

prioritized_data_gaps.rationale: Referee data is ALREADY in the CSV files (2019-2023) but completely unused. Different referees have statistically significant tendencies for cards, penalties, and fouls which can affect match outcomes. This is the easiest possible data addition — just read an existing column.

experiment_design.treatment: Add referee identity (encoded) + referee historical card/penalty rate
experiment_design.methodology: Temporal OOS, windows where referee data is available
experiment_design.success_criterion: Any LL improvement in Football-only model

prioritized_data_gaps.rationale: days_since_last_match exists but is a crude proxy. A team playing 3 matches in 7 days (Champions League + League) is at a disadvantage vs a rested opponent. Fixture congestion can be computed from the existing date data. The current feature only captures the LAST match gap, not cumulative fatigue.

experiment_design.treatment: Replace days_since_last_match with: matches_in_last_7d, matches_in_last_14d, rest_days_vs_opponent, cumulative_minutes_estimate

prioritized_data_gaps.estimated_cost: FREE (StatsBomb open) to VERY HIGH (Opta enterprise)
prioritized_data_gaps.historical_availability: Limited (StatsBomb open data: specific tournaments only)
prioritized_data_gaps.coverage: Limited open data; enterprise requires license
prioritized_data_gaps.rationale: Event-level data is the foundation for computing real xG, xT, PPDA, and all advanced metrics. However, free historical coverage is limited. This is a long-term investment rather than a quick win. Understat provides match-level xG which is a practical intermediate step.

experiment_design.baseline: Best model after Understat xG integration
experiment_design.treatment: Replace Understat xG with StatsBomb/Opta event-level computed xG
experiment_design.methodology: Temporal OOS on available data only

prioritized_data_gaps.rationale: Weather affects playing conditions (rain, wind, extreme temperatures). However, bookmakers likely account for weather, and the effect size is small. Low priority but easy to implement once venue coordinates are available.

experiment_design.treatment: Add temperature, wind_speed, precipitation_binary at kickoff time

data_quality_contract.principle: NO FABRICATION. Every feature must have traceable provenance.

feature_states.REAL: Directly measured or officially recorded value (e.g., goals scored, Pinnacle closing odds, referee name)
feature_states.PROXY: Derived from a correlated but different measurement (e.g., xG_PROXY = shots_on_target * 0.1). MUST be labeled with _PROXY suffix and MUST NEVER be presented as the real metric.
feature_states.DERIVED: Computed from REAL data using a defensible method (e.g., ELO rating, attacking_strength, form_points). Method must be documented.
feature_states.MISSING: Data point is not available. Must be represented as null/NaN, never imputed silently. Model must handle missing values explicitly.
feature_states.STALE: Data is available but older than the freshness threshold (e.g., injury data from 3 weeks ago). Must carry staleness timestamp.
feature_states.UNAVAILABLE: Data source does not provide this field for this match/league/season. Distinct from MISSING (which implies the field exists but is absent for a specific observation).

required_metadata_per_feature.source: The data source or computation method that produced this value
required_metadata_per_feature.timestamp: When the value was recorded or computed
required_metadata_per_feature.observation_time: The time period the value represents (e.g., 'last 10 matches before 2024-03-15')
required_metadata_per_feature.freshness: Time between observation and prediction time
required_metadata_per_feature.provenance: Chain of derivation from raw data to feature value
required_metadata_per_feature.quality_state: One of: REAL, PROXY, DERIVED, MISSING, STALE, UNAVAILABLE

data_quality_contract.proxy_labeling_rule: A proxy feature MUST include _PROXY in its name. Example: xG_PROXY (current), not xG. When real xG is acquired, the proxy feature is retired and the real feature takes the canonical name xG.
data_quality_contract.missing_data_rule: Missing values MUST be represented as null/NaN. Default imputation is FORBIDDEN without explicit documentation of the method and its justification. Tree-based models can handle NaN natively.
data_quality_contract.historical_reproducibility_rule: Any feature used in training must be reproducible from raw data. No ad-hoc adjustments. The Phase 2 pipeline is the canonical feature computation path.

predictive_value_experiment_protocol.core_principle: Do not assume data improves prediction. Measure it.

required_experiments_per_data_addition.name: football_only_incremental
required_experiments_per_data_addition.description: Add new data to football-only features, measure against football-only baseline

required_experiments_per_data_addition.name: combined_incremental
required_experiments_per_data_addition.description: Add new data to combined features, measure against combined baseline

required_experiments_per_data_addition.name: market_comparison
required_experiments_per_data_addition.description: The critical test: does the new data help beat the market?
required_experiments_per_data_addition.treatment: Best model configuration with new data
required_experiments_per_data_addition.success_criterion: Must beat market in at least 3/5 temporal windows on log loss

methodology.xgboost_params: Same hyperparameters as Phase 3.5 (max_depth=5, eta=0.05, subsample=0.8, colsample_bytree=0.8, min_child_weight=5, gamma=0.1, lambda=1.5, alpha=0.1, early_stopping_rounds=100)
methodology.leakage_prevention: STRICT: all features for match at date T must use only data from dates < T. New data sources must be backfilled with correct temporal ordering.

predictive_value_experiment_protocol.retention_criterion: A data source is only retained if it demonstrates meaningful out-of-sample improvement (LL > 0.005) over the baseline in at least 2/5 temporal windows, OR provides another clearly justified product capability (e.g., displaying real xG in the UI even if it doesn't improve LL).

future_flow: EXTERNAL SOURCES (API-Football, Understat, Odds API, ESPN, football-data.co.uk, weather APIs)
-> INGESTION (scheduled + on-demand collectors, rate limiting, error handling)
-> RAW STORAGE (PostgreSQL: matches, odds, injuries, events tables)
-> NORMALIZATION (team name mapping, league mapping, date standardization)
-> PROVENANCE (source, timestamp, quality state, observation_time for every data point)
-> FEATURE STORE (canonical 50+ features with full metadata per Data Quality Contract)
-> MODEL FEATURES (features selected for each model, with feature_states documented)
-> ELASTICO (API response with full provenance chain)
-> USER (probability display, market edge, confidence, data quality indicators)
data_architecture.current_gap: The current system jumps from EXTERNAL SOURCES directly to MODEL FEATURES with no intermediate storage, provenance tracking, or quality control. The database schema exists (14 tables) but is completely unwired.

risks.description: Understat is an unofficial source that could change or disappear without notice. Scraping may break.
risks.mitigation: Cache all scraped data locally. Have fbref as backup source. Design feature pipeline to handle source failures gracefully.

risks.description: Free tier allows 100 requests/day. Historical backfill for injuries across 5 leagues x 5 seasons requires thousands of requests.
risks.mitigation: Use paid tier for backfill, free tier for ongoing. Implement caching and batch requests.

risks.description: Injury news, lineups, and odds movement data have timing components. Using post-match injury data or closing odds movement as pre-match features would introduce leakage.
risks.mitigation: Every new feature must pass the temporal leakage test: feature value at time T must only use information available at time T. Document observation_time for every feature.

risks.description: Adding more features to XGBoost may increase overfitting (as seen in Phase 3.5 where 46 football features underperformed 4 market features).
risks.mitigation: Each feature addition must be tested incrementally. Use strict temporal OOS. If new features hurt, remove them. Feature selection is part of the experiment protocol.

risks.description: Even with perfect data, bookmaker closing odds may still be superior. The efficient market hypothesis suggests the market already incorporates most available information.
risks.mitigation: The goal is not guaranteed market-beating predictions but a defensible, empirically-validated system. If data additions improve calibration or provide product value (UI display) even without beating the market, they may still be worthwhile.
risks.note: This is the core strategic risk. Phase 5 showed the market LL is 0.959. Beating this requires genuinely new information.

risks.risk: No improvement even after data additions
risks.description: If experiments show that even with real xG + injuries + lineups, ELASTICO still cannot beat raw market odds, the project must accept that the market is the best available predictor.
risks.mitigation: This is a valid outcome. ELASTICO can still provide value by: (1) displaying calibrated market probabilities, (2) showing football analysis (real xG, ELO, form) alongside market odds, (3) detecting market timing signals, (4) providing a comprehensive analytics platform. Not beating the market is not the same as having no value.

recommended_phase_7.title: Data Advantage Execution
recommended_phase_7.approach: Stop model development. Acquire and integrate data. Test each addition empirically.
recommended_phase_7.first_experiment: Extract unused CSV data (opening odds, referee) and test odds movement + referee features
recommended_phase_7.second_experiment: Integrate Understat xG and replace xG_PROXY. Test with Football-only and Combined models.
recommended_phase_7.third_experiment: Wire API-Football injuries endpoint. Test injury features.
recommended_phase_7.success_gate: Only proceed to next data addition if the current one shows measurable OOS improvement.
recommended_phase_7.failure_mode: If no data addition beats the market after 3 experiments, accept market-calibrated display as the product's prediction backbone and focus on analytics/UX value.
do_not: Fabricate or proxy any new features
